sets.title: Colloquial Recognition
sets.description: Identify reduced forms, particles, and colloquial register features
sets.descriptionRussian: Определите разговорные формы, частицы и особенности устной речи

items.prompt: What is the colloquial reduction of сейчас?
items.promptEnglish: This is one of the most common casual reductions in spoken Russian.
items.hint: The vowels collapse and the consonants shift to щ.
items.explanation: Сейчас → щас is the standard colloquial reduction. You hear it constantly in casual speech.

items.prompt: Чё ты делаешь? - What does чё replace?
items.promptEnglish: This is informal and would sound rude in formal settings.
items.hint: The standard neutral question word gets shortened to one syllable.
items.explanation: Что → чё (or чо) is extremely common in casual speech. It sounds blunt or rude in formal contexts.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses a typical colloquial ellipsis (omitted words)?
items.promptEnglish: Incomplete sentences are normal in spoken Russian.
items.hint: In casual speech, you drop the verb entirely when the meaning is obvious.
items.explanation: Мне кофе. (= Дайте мне кофе / Мне, пожалуйста, кофе.) The verb is implied. This is standard at cafes and restaurants.

items.prompt: Ну, я не знаю... - What function does ну serve here?
items.promptEnglish: Ну is one of the most versatile Russian particles.
items.hint: Like 'well...' or 'um...' in English when you're not sure what to say.
items.explanation: Ну as a hesitation marker: 'Well, I don't know...' It softens the uncertainty, like English 'well' or 'um.'

items.prompt: Ты же знаешь! - What does же add?
items.promptEnglish: Же is a particle that modifies the emotional weight of the sentence.
items.hint: The speaker is reminding the listener of something they should already know.
items.explanation: Же adds emphatic force: 'You DO know!' or 'You know this already!' It reminds the listener of a known fact.

items.prompt: Вот этот, справа. - What does вот do here?
items.promptEnglish: A particle used when pointing something out.
items.hint: Like pointing with your finger: 'This one right here.'
items.explanation: Вот = 'here,' 'this one,' 'right here.' It draws attention to something specific, like pointing.

items.prompt: Я-то знаю, а ты? - What does -то express?
items.promptEnglish: A suffix particle that highlights contrast.
items.hint: The speaker separates themselves from someone else: 'I, for one...'
items.explanation: The particle -то highlights contrast: 'I (for my part) know, but what about you?' It sets the speaker apart.

items.prompt: Which is a colloquial diminutive form of минута?
items.promptEnglish: Diminutives soften the tone in casual speech.
items.hint: The -ка suffix is one of the most common diminutive endings for feminine nouns.
items.explanation: Минутка (a little minute) sounds softer and more friendly. Подождите минутку! sounds much warmer than Подождите минуту!

items.prompt: Тебе чаёк налить? - What does чаёк convey compared to чай?
items.promptEnglish: Notice the suffix on the word for tea.
items.hint: The -ёк diminutive suffix makes the offer sound cozy and informal.
items.explanation: Чаёк is the affectionate diminutive of чай. It makes the offer warmer: 'Shall I pour you some nice tea?' Very homey and casual.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these into Standard (neutral/formal) vs Colloquial (informal/spoken)

sets.title: Particle Practice
sets.description: Master the colloquial particles: ну, же, вот, -то
sets.descriptionRussian: Отработайте разговорные частицы: ну, же, вот, -то

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Well, I'm not sure... (speaker is hesitating)
minimalPairs.explanation: Ну as a hesitation filler: 'Well, I'm not sure...' Like English 'well' or 'um' at the start of a thought.

minimalPairs.context: _____ он, смотри! (pointing someone out in a crowd)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There he is, look! (pointing at someone)
minimalPairs.explanation: Вот for pointing: 'There he is!' Drawing attention to something you can see or identify.

minimalPairs.context: Я-_____ всё сделал, а Коля ничего. (contrast: I did it, but Kolya didn't)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I, for one, did everything, but Kolya did nothing.
minimalPairs.explanation: The particle -то highlights contrast: 'I (for my part) did everything.' It separates the speaker's action from Kolya's inaction.

minimalPairs.context: Мы _____ договорились вчера! Ты забыл? (emphatic reminder)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: We DID agree yesterday! Did you forget?
minimalPairs.explanation: Же for emphatic reminder: 'We DID agree!' The speaker is frustrated the listener forgot.
Ну for impatient urging: 'Come on!' Here ну pushes the listener to act, similar to English 'come on' or 'well, let's go.'

minimalPairs.context: _____ так и живём. (summing up a situation: 'that's how it is')
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: So that's how we live. (a resigned summary)
minimalPairs.explanation: Вот for summing up or concluding: 'So that's how it is.' Вот так = 'like that, that's how.'

blanks: Ты _____ обещал помочь! Почему не пришёл? (You DID promise!)
_____, я даже не знаю, что сказать... (Well, I don't even know what to say...)
Деньги-_____ есть, а времени нет. (Money I have, but time I don't.)
_____ мой новый телефон, смотри! (Here's my new phone, look!)
_____ ладно, я согласен. (Well, okay, I agree.)
explanations: Же emphasizes the reminder: 'You DID promise!' The speaker is holding the listener accountable.
Ну as a hesitation filler: 'Well...' The speaker is gathering their thoughts.
-То highlights contrast: 'Money, for its part, I have, but...' Setting up a contrast.
Вот for presenting: 'Here it is!' Drawing attention to the phone.
Ну for casual transition into agreement: 'Well, okay then.'

items.prompt: Ну ты даёшь! - This expression means:
items.hint: This is an idiomatic expression of surprise or amazement at someone's actions.
items.explanation: Ну ты даёшь! = 'Wow!' or 'You're really something!' An expression of amazement (positive or negative) at what someone did.

items.prompt: Which particle would you add: 'Книга-_____ интересная, но длинная.' (The book IS interesting, but long.)
items.promptEnglish: Conceding a point before introducing a 'but.'
items.hint: Concessive contrast: 'The book, for its part, IS interesting, but...'
items.explanation: Книга-то интересная = 'The book IS interesting (I'll give you that), but...' The -то concedes one point before contrasting.

items.prompt: А вот и нет! - This expression is used to:
items.hint: Like saying 'No way!' or 'That's not true!' in response to someone.
items.explanation: А вот и нет! = 'No, that's not so!' or 'Nuh-uh!' A casual, often playful contradiction. The opposite: А вот и да! = 'Yes it is!'

sets.title: Build and Translate
sets.description: Build colloquial sentences and translate casual expressions
sets.descriptionRussian: Постройте разговорные предложения и переведите выражения

translation.hint: Start with the hesitation particle ну, then может (casual form of может быть)
Use же after the subject for emphatic force

translation.english: Two coffees, please. (casual cafe order, no verb)
translation.hint: Drop the verb entirely; just the quantity + noun + please

translation.english: I'll be right there! (casual, using reduced form)
translation.hint: Use the colloquial reduction of сейчас + perfective verb

translation.english: The weather IS nice, but it's cold. (concessive contrast)
translation.hint: Use -то on the topic noun to concede the point before contrasting

translation.english: So basically, she's not coming. (casual summary)
translation.hint: Start with the discourse marker that means 'long story short'

items.prompt: Короче, я опоздал. - What does короче function as?
items.promptEnglish: One of the most common casual discourse markers.
options: A filler meaning 'basically' or 'long story short'
items.answer: A filler meaning 'basically' or 'long story short'
items.hint: It signals the speaker is cutting to the main point.
items.explanation: Короче = 'in short, basically, long story short.' Extremely common filler/discourse marker. Короче, я опоздал = 'So basically, I was late.'

items.prompt: Типа он не знал. - Типа here means:
items.promptEnglish: A casual filler word younger speakers use heavily.
items.hint: Similar to how English speakers overuse 'like' in casual speech.
items.explanation: Типа = 'like, supposedly, sort of.' Типа он не знал = 'Like, he supposedly didn't know.' Very common in casual youth speech.

items.promptEnglish: A colloquial exclamation (ничё = reduced form of ничего).
items.hint: It literally means 'not bad for oneself' but is used as an exclamation.
items.explanation: Ничё себе! (from ничего себе!) = 'Wow!' or 'No way!' An exclamation of surprise. Ничё is the casual reduction of ничего.

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: All colloquial register features in varied formats
sets.descriptionRussian: Все особенности разговорной речи в разных форматах

items.prompt: Ну вот, опять двадцать пять! - This colloquial expression means:
items.promptEnglish: A common idiom with two particles at the start.
options: Here we go again! (frustration at repetition)
items.answer: Here we go again! (frustration at repetition)
items.hint: The speaker is annoyed that the same thing is happening yet again.
items.explanation: Ну вот, опять двадцать пять! = 'Here we go again!' Expresses frustration at a recurring problem. Двадцать пять (25) is just part of the idiom.

items.prompt: Which is the most natural casual response to 'Пойдём в кино?'
items.promptEnglish: Someone suggests going to the movies.
options: Конечно, я с удовольствием приму ваше приглашение.
items.hint: The most casual and natural response among friends.
items.explanation: Ну давай! = 'Sure, let's do it!' Very natural, casual agreement. Да, пойдём is also fine but slightly less colloquial.

items.prompt: Ой, забыл совсем! - What does ой express?
items.hint: Like 'Oh!' or 'Oops!' when you suddenly remember something.
items.explanation: Ой = 'Oh! Oops!' Mild surprise or alarm. Ой, забыл! = 'Oh, I forgot!' It can also express mild pain (stubbing a toe) or surprise.

items.prompt: Ему-то хорошо, а мне? - The -то here signals:
items.promptEnglish: Notice who -то is attached to and what follows.
items.hint: The speaker contrasts his situation with the other person's.
items.explanation: Ему-то хорошо, а мне? = 'HE's fine, but what about ME?' The -то marks ему as the contrasted element.

errorCorrection.sentence: Сейчас приду! (in a very casual text message to a close friend)
errorCorrection.hint: In a casual text to a friend, the full form sounds overly formal.
errorCorrection.explanation: In casual texting, щас is the natural choice. Сейчас is correct but sounds more neutral/formal.

errorCorrection.sentence: Она сказала: «Я приду позже.» (retelling the conversation very casually)
errorCorrection.hint: In casual retelling, young speakers replace speech verbs with такой/такая.
errorCorrection.explanation: Она такая: «Я приду позже.» Using такая to introduce speech is very colloquial storytelling style.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Well, okay, I'll go. (giving in reluctantly)
minimalPairs.explanation: Ну for reluctant concession: 'Well, fine, I'll go.' The speaker is giving in after hesitation.

minimalPairs.context: _____ так всегда бывает. (summing up a situation: 'that's how it always is')
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: That's how it always goes. (a resigned conclusion)
minimalPairs.explanation: Вот так = 'that's how.' Summing up or concluding: 'That's how it always goes.' A resigned or philosophical observation.

minimalPairs.context: Работа-_____ есть, но скучная. (The work exists, I'll grant you that, but...)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There IS work, I admit, but it's boring.
minimalPairs.explanation: -То for concessive contrast: 'Work, there IS, but it's boring.' Conceding one point before the contrast.

minimalPairs.context: Он _____ сам всё знает! Зачем ему помогать? (He DOES know everything himself!)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He knows it all himself! Why help him?
minimalPairs.explanation: Же for emphatic assertion: 'He DOES know it all!' Emphasizing a known fact to support the argument.

blanks: _____, я опоздал, извини. (Long story short, I was late.)
Она _____: «Не хочу!» (She goes: 'I don't want to!' - casual retelling)
_____ приду, подожди! (I'll be right there! - casual reduction)
Погода-_____ ничего, но ветер сильный. (The weather IS okay, but the wind is strong.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Mixed colloquial features: discourse markers, speech verbs, reductions, contrast particles
hints: The discourse marker that means 'basically' or 'in short.'
Casual storytelling verb for 'she goes / she's like.'
Contrast particle conceding a point before 'but.'
explanations: Короче = 'long story short, basically.' Sets up a casual summary.
Такая replaces сказала in casual retelling: 'She's like: I don't want to!'
Щас = сейчас in casual speech. Щас приду! = 'Be right there!'
-То concedes the point: 'The weather IS okay (I'll give you that), but...'
